purpose: Interferon Beta-1A is used to treat relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (MS). It helps reduce the number of MS flare-ups (relapses) and can slow down the worsening of the disease. It does not cure MS, but it can help you feel better and have fewer attacks.
how_it_works: Your immune system normally uses proteins called interferons to help regulate itself. In MS, the immune system mistakenly attacks the protective coating around your nerve fibers. Interferon Beta-1A works by calming down this overactive immune response, helping to reduce inflammation and protect your nerves from damage.
common_side_effects: Flu-like symptoms such as fever, chills, muscle aches, and tiredness — especially after your injection (these often get better over time). Redness, swelling, or soreness at the injection site. Headache. Feeling weak or fatigued. Nausea. Some people may notice changes in their blood counts or liver enzymes, which is why regular blood tests are important.
warnings: Tell your doctor if you feel very depressed or have any thoughts of harming yourself, as this medication can sometimes affect mood. Let your doctor know if you have liver problems, thyroid issues, seizures, heart problems, or if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Do not skip blood tests — your doctor needs to monitor your liver and blood regularly. Avoid this medication if you are allergic to interferon beta or human albumin.
typical_dosing: The dose depends on which brand you are using. Avonex is usually given as one injection into a muscle (thigh or upper arm) once a week. Rebif is usually given as an injection under the skin three times a week, with doses starting low and gradually increasing. Your healthcare team will show you how to give yourself the injection safely at home.
